relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project-code parse step on the vulnerable path: `processPacket()` materializes the attacker-controlled IEC-104 APDU length and PDU type that drive the later branch and offset arithmetic.

Insufficient guard. After `offset` has already been advanced by `len + 2`, the code still uses only `len >= 6` to justify the later `asdu` read and never checks whether six bytes remain from the new `offset` to `payload_len`.
AddressSanitizer sink. This statement reads a 16-bit ASDU value from `payload[4 + offset]` after `offset` has been advanced past the currently admitted bytes.

nodes.state: The mutation `offset += len + 2` creates the post-ASDU cursor that the later guard and sink both reuse. On the crashing APDU this advance moves `offset` to 179; on the fixed boundary witness it moves `offset` to the exact safe boundary value 171.
nodes.evidence: The curated traces record `asdu_cursor_advance.offset_after_advance=179` on the vulnerable original and `171` on the fixed boundary witness, and the transition assertion verifies that same value reaches the next guard site unchanged.

edges.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `asdu_cursor_advance.offset_after_advance == post_asdu_guard.offset == 179`, and the fixed boundary witness preserves the same equality at 171 when the protected read genuinely executes.
The vulnerable original trace records `post_asdu_guard.offset == asdu_read_sink.offset == 179`, and the fixed boundary witness preserves that equality at 171 when the sink runs safely.
